title: Intelligent region & tier routing with budgeted GPU fallback cascade
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Background:
Redwood needs an operator-friendly policy that routes inference requests across regions, customer tiers, and GPU families while respecting per-customer and global budget caps. Current behavior is reactive: when capacity or price spikes occur we fall back to a single low-cost variant. This causes abrupt quality shifts and hard outages for traffic-heavy customers.

Goal:
1) Implement a cost-aware routing policy that considers spot vs on-demand pricing, GPU family suitability for a model, and per-customer daily/weekly soft budget buckets.
2) Provide a configurable cascade of fallback actions that preserve perceived output quality: e.g., route to compatible GPU family, switch to quantized model variant, apply adaptive batching, then finally route to spot with reduced tokens.
3) Add operator controls in Console for budget windows, burst credits, and probabilistic spillover to spot pools.

Non-goals:
- Full multi-cloud placement (this ticket focuses on region selection within existing cloud accounts).
- Model training changes.

Design summary:
- Policy DSL: introduce a compact routing policy expression attached to a customer route. Example: 
  priority: [region:us-west-2, tier:dedicated, gpu:A100]
  budget_window: daily
  soft_cap: $500
  burst_tokens: 20
  fallback_sequence: [same-arch-quantized, lower-seq-len, spot-prob=0.3, model-variant-b]

- Scoring & decision: For each incoming request compute a score for candidate placements: score = w_cost*cost_score + w_latency*latency_score + w_sla*sla_score + w_compat*compat_score. Cost estimates use real-time spot/on-demand price feeds and per-model token cost profiles.

- Burst credits: Allow short bursts beyond soft_cap using a token bucket (burst_tokens). When burst exhausted, degrade along fallback_sequence instead of immediate hard reject.

- Probabilistic spot spillover: To protect latency SLOs, poll a spot pool with a configurable spill probability. If spot queueing increases above threshold, reduce prob and surface a warning to Console.

- GPU family scoring: Maintain a per-model compatibility profile that ranks GPU families by expected latency and cost (e.g., H100-int8 > A100-fp16 > T4-int8 for X model). Use cached inference microbenchmarks to populate the profile.

- Console & API: New route config fields (budget_window, soft_cap, burst_tokens, fallback_sequence, spot_spill_prob). Console UI to visualize daily budget burn, predicted cost for candidate placements, and recent spill events.

Telemetry & safety:
- Emit routing_decision events with reason, scores, and cost delta estimation.
- Add regression checks: latency P95 and quality regression by prompt set for any runtime change.
- Safety net: a per-customer hard_cap that prevents routing to spot pools if set to "never_spill".

Rollout plan:
1) Implement policy engine and scoring in runtime behind feature flag.
2) Add Console controls and basic visualizations (read-only at first).
3) Canary: route 5% of small customers through new policies with monitoring.
4) Expand to 25% then full after 2 weeks of stable metrics.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs operator control: DSL kept minimal to reduce misconfiguration risk.
- Cost accuracy vs latency: price lookups cached for 30s to avoid per-request overhead.
- Quality preservation: prefer quantized-compatible variants and reduced seq-length before switching model family.

Acceptance criteria:
- Runtime can evaluate policy DSL and pick placements with a stable scoring model under load (>= 10k rps test).
- Console exposes budget burn and allows toggling spill probability per customer.
- Burst token behavior honored under synthetic overrun test: soft_cap exceeded but traffic allowed up to burst_tokens with fallback sequence applied afterwards.
- No regression in latency P95 beyond 10% for canary customers; quality QA shows <2% degradation on acceptance prompt set.

Implementation notes / TODOs:
- Metric: routing.cost_estimate, routing.choice_reason, routing.fallback_stage, customer.budget_remaining.
- Integration PRs: runtime policy evaluator, pricing feed adapter, console UI, e2e test harness.
- Security: ensure pricing feeds and policy configs are audited in change logs.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha Kaur: Created ticket after ops incident where a high-spend customer was abruptly moved to a low-quality spot variant during a regional price spike. Goal is to provide smoother degradation and operator visibility.

2026-02-24 - Diego Martinez: Spiked a prototype scorer in staging using historical price traces. Initial results show 12% cost savings with 1% latency regression at P95 when using quantized variants as first fallback.
2026-03-02 - Design review (Lina Park): Suggested adding burst_tokens and explicit hard_cap to give customers predictable spend ceilings. Added to spec.
2026-03-05 - Ops (Harper Singh): Ran chaos test with simulated spot pool drain; observed that probabilistic spill reduced spot queue length but increased variance in P95. Need tuning knob in Console.
2026-03-09 - Diego Martinez: Opened draft PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1423 (policy engine + scoring). Linked to console feature branch. Next: integrate pricing feed and acceptance tests.
2026-03-10 - QA (Nina Patel): Added e2e test plan and sample prompt set for quality regression checks. Marking In Progress.
2026-03-12 - Note: targeting staged canary on 2026-03-18 pending infra sign-off and pricing feed rate limit adjustments.
acceptance_criteria: Policy evaluator returns placement and fallback decision with provenance fields for every request (reason, scores, estimated_cost)
Console shows per-customer soft_cap, hard_cap, burst_tokens, and current burn for the day
Burst credit behavior allows short overrun while ensuring subsequent requests follow fallback_sequence
Canary customers (5%) experience <10% P95 latency regression and <2% quality regression on acceptance prompt set
Operator can disable spot spill per-customer via hard_cap or 'never_spill' flag
